title: fix(cli): format created key permissions
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
- Reuses the key-list formatter so human key-create output shows readable permissions instead of [object Object].
- Preserves raw permission objects in JSON and existing null handling.
- Adds actual-command regressions: old source fails four; fixed 11 pass. Parent reran all 11. Full CLI suite: 291 pass; build and Biome pass.
- Strict typecheck reports the same 36 baseline diagnostics. Local cached Vitest is 2.1.9 versus declared 3.x.

Fixes #16384

gist.headline: Keys, minus the mystery objects
gist.blurb: Creating a key gets readable permissions in the CLI instead of the deeply informative `[object Object]`. JSON output keeps the raw permission objects.
gist.summary: The polli CLI reuses its key-list formatter for human-readable key-create permissions, replacing `[object Object]` while preserving raw permission objects in JSON output and existing null handling.
gist.impact: CLI users get readable permissions when creating a key; scripts consuming JSON continue to receive the original permission objects.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the polli CLI as a cozy retro terminal showing a newly created key and tidy permission lines, with a small key-shaped code-plant nearby. Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, points out the readable output.
